title: use-after-free of the decompressor input buffer after a MemoryError (CVE-2026-6100)
consumer: zlib._ZlibDecompressor.decompress after a forced MemoryError; Modules/zlibmodule.c
live_proof: measured 2026-10-29 on p13 with a fixed/buggy differential. On the pinned 3.13.7 ASan build (--with-address-sanitizer, pymalloc off, gcc 15.2) with PYTHONMALLOC=malloc and ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=0: ASAN:memcpy-param-overlap, the overlapping-source memcpy at decompress (Modules/zlibmodule.c:1585) reached from zlib_ZlibDecompressor_decompress_impl -- the stale input pointer the next decompress() reuses. A second build of the same tree with the upstream fix applied (self->zst.next_in = NULL at decompress()'s error label, commit 8fc66aef6d) runs the trigger to its end with no report. Under PYTHONMALLOC=pymalloc the report does not survive, so the damage stays inside the arena.
fidelity: interpreter-trigger, real allocator. Upstream's own regression test body (gh-154713, commit 5bcd67189b, Lib/test/test_zlib.py test_decompress_memoryerror_no_dangling_input) driven through the real CPython. The allocation-failure injector is CPython's own pyfailmalloc set_nomemory/remove_mem_hooks: _testcapi on the host oracle, and the verbatim-copied _capstone_nomemory module in the capstone image (the build omits the 32-file _testcapi). The injector is harness scaffolding; the defect is zlibmodule.c, the pinned release's own code. There is no C-model sibling: pymalloc-repros/07 models this defect's allocator sequence, but the trigger here is the interpreter reaching it.

virtual-malloc.oracle: virtual profile, pymalloc stock on musl mallocng (tools/arms.json virtual-cpython): a fault in one of the case's fault_sites, or the trigger ends and this arm did not see it

virtual-nested-pools.oracle: virtual profile, pymalloc's blocks as child lifetimes (patch 0014, CDERIVE/CREVOKE; tools/arms.json virtual-cpython-pools): as virtual-malloc

cheribsd-revocation.oracle: completion while the block's arena stays live: pymalloc links the freed block onto its own pool free list, so the platform has no free to revoke. Once pymalloc returns an emptied arena to the system allocator (insert_to_freepool, when nf == ao->ntotalpools && ao->nextarena != NULL) the platform does have a free, and after a revocation sweep the stale access faults with SIGPROT si_code=2 (PROT_CHERI_TAG). Both outcomes are admissible; which one occurs depends on arena occupancy and sweep timing rather than on the defect, so this arm does not separate these cases. A bounds fault (si_code=1) would falsify this.

status: live and its layer measured on the host with a fixed/buggy differential (2026-10-29); first Capstone reading in results/2026-10-29-virtual, beside the corpus's verdict_bundles and not derived into this file: virtual-malloc MISSED (completes), virtual-nested-pools CAUGHT (cause 25 in memcpy, its host fault site). cheribsd-revocation has not run it
layer_note: measured 2026-10-29: the heap-overlap report under PYTHONMALLOC=malloc does not survive PYTHONMALLOC=pymalloc on a second 3.13.7 build with ASan and pymalloc both on (configure's --with-address-sanitizer forces pymalloc off): the decompressor's input buffer is PyMem_Malloc memory, a pymalloc block, and the stale read stays inside it.
fault_sites_why: Host ASan (CPython 3.13.7 --with-address-sanitizer, PYTHONMALLOC=malloc, results/2026-10-29-asan/sites.tsv) reports memcpy-param-overlap at memcpy sanitizer_common_interceptors_memintrinsics.inc:117 | memcpy string_fortified.h:29 | decompress Modules/zlibmodule.c:1585 | zlib_ZlibDecompressor_decompress_impl Modules/zlibmodule.c:1690 | zlib_ZlibDecompressor_decompress Modules/clinic/zlibmodule.c.h:964. That run uses no Capstone arm and was recorded before any virtual arm ran.
